# lambda-trigger-dynamodb

Creates a DynamoDB Streams event source mapping that invokes a Lambda function when items are created, updated, or deleted in a DynamoDB table.

## Usage

```hcl
module "stream_trigger" {
  source = "../../modules/lambda-trigger-dynamodb"

  function_name = module.my_function.function_name
  function_arn  = module.my_function.function_arn
  role_name     = module.my_function.role_name
  stream_arn    = aws_dynamodb_table.orders.stream_arn
}
```

## IAM Model

This is a **pull-based** trigger. Lambda polls the DynamoDB stream, so the execution role needs permission to read from it. The module attaches a policy granting `dynamodb:GetRecords`, `dynamodb:GetShardIterator`, `dynamodb:DescribeStream`, and `dynamodb:ListStreams` to the provided `role_name`.

This means `role_name` is required (unlike push-based triggers). Use the core module's `role_name` output.

## Inputs

### Required

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `function_name` | `string` | Name of the Lambda function. Used for resource naming. |
| `function_arn` | `string` | ARN of the Lambda function. Used by the event source mapping. |
| `role_name` | `string` | Name of the Lambda execution role. The module attaches a DynamoDB stream read policy to this role. Must not be `null` — use the core module's `role_name` output (which is non-null when the module creates the role). |
| `stream_arn` | `string` | ARN of the DynamoDB stream. The table must have `stream_enabled = true` with `stream_view_type` set (e.g. `NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES`). |

### Optional

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `starting_position` | `string` | `"LATEST"` | Position in the stream where Lambda starts reading. Possible values: `"LATEST"` (only new records after creation), `"TRIM_HORIZON"` (from the oldest available record). |
| `batch_size` | `number` | `100` | Maximum number of records per batch sent to the Lambda function. Range: `1` to `10000`. Larger batches improve throughput but increase per-invocation latency. |
| `maximum_batching_window_in_seconds` | `number` | `0` | Maximum time in seconds to gather records before invoking the function. Range: `0` to `300`. Set to `0` (default) for immediate invocation once a record is available. Values above `0` enable batching windows, which reduce invocations at the cost of latency. |
| `parallelization_factor` | `number` | `1` | Number of batches to process concurrently from each shard. Range: `1` to `10`. Increasing this value processes more records in parallel but may cause out-of-order processing within a shard. |
| `filter_criteria` | `list(object)` | `[]` | Event filtering criteria. Each object has a `pattern` field containing a JSON-encoded filter pattern. Only records matching at least one pattern are sent to the function. See [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-eventfiltering.html) for pattern syntax. |
| `tags` | `map(string)` | `{}` | Map of tags applied to all resources. |

**`filter_criteria` object fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `pattern` | `string` | JSON-encoded filter pattern. Example: `jsonencode({"eventName": ["INSERT"]})` to only process new items. |

## Outputs

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `event_source_mapping_id` | ID of the Lambda event source mapping. |
